steps: Plan location, floor & fuel

Choose a level spot that can carry the stove and venting, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies, with room behind it to remove the fan. Settle the vent path before framing, and convert to propane before installing.

• Determine the vent path and termination type (vertical or horizontal, sections 5.0 and 6.0) before framing. For a horizontal termination, frame the wall pass-through per the rough-in step.
  • Locate electrical (if needed) and the gas line; finish any material below or around the stove location; place and secure the stove; install the vent system.
  • Floor: set the stove directly on wood or a non-combustible surface (not linoleum or carpet) covering its entire width and depth. On carpet, tile or other combustible material other than wood flooring, install it on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth. Above floor level, build a solid, continuous platform.
  • Approved for bedrooms. Expect a large amount of heat when choosing the spot, and leave space between the back of the stove and the wall to remove the fan for maintenance.
  • Propane: it is easier to convert before installing — LXL-22-L per its conversion kit manual (kit number: see the Fuel & conversion spec), LXL-22-MV per the #OCK-S190A kit manual.
  • Hold the Table 3.1 clearances (Clearances spec).
Vent rough-in & wall pass-through

Measure from the stove's floor level to the center of the vent penetration, frame the opening so the vent runs level through the wall pass-through, and fit wall thimbles that keep 1" clearance to combustibles.

• This is a cold air transfer area: comply with all clearances and local building codes, and insulate outside walls to keep cold air out of the room.
  • The minimum horizontal rough-in is drawn in Figure 3.2 (p. 13) for a Simpson DuraVent 4" x 6-5/8" elbow. Other makers' elbows vary in height, so adjust the rough opening to keep clearances.
  • Clearances: 1" on all sides of vertical pipe; 1" at the top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe; 2-1/4" from the top of horizontal pipe to the ceiling; 1" on all surfaces of the pipe after the wall pass-through.
  • Wall thimbles meeting the 1" clearances are required wherever a horizontal run passes through an interior or exterior wall. Thimbles and attic insulation shields may be insulated with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136.
  • Horizontal sections: 1/4" rise for every 12" of travel. Terminate per section 5.2 and don't recess the vent cap into the wall or siding.
Alcove, masonry or outdoor installs

Alcove: frame to Figures 3.3 and 3.4, with an 8" maximum mantel projection. Masonry: the stove sits inside the existing fireplace, with set mantel heights. Outdoor covered: protected from direct precipitation, operation approved from 40°F to 110°F.

• Alcove (Figures 3.3–3.4, pp. 14–15, drawn only): a front wall may hide the vent pipe and elbow as long as clearances are met. An 8" mantel is the maximum projection allowed in any alcove installation. Keep minimum clearances for air circulation around the stove and venting.
  • Masonry application (Figure 3.5, p. 16): 3/4" mantel trim may start at 40-1/2" and a 6" mantel at 44" above the floor. Combustibles at the sides in front (mantel leg, sidewall) stay 3" from the masonry opening, with unlimited projection. Each extra 1" of mantel projection needs 1" more height. For venting through the chimney, see the Venting spec.
  • Outdoor covered (pp. 17–18): calculate the roof overhang from Figure 3.6 (drawn only); don't interrupt the continuous insulated building envelope or weatherproof membrane (Figure 3.7); wiring to the outdoor requirements of NFPA 70. Black-painted safety barriers are highly recommended — plated or patina finishes oxidize and discolor.
Note: p. 16 gives the masonry mantel heights as a 6" mantel at 44" above the floor, with 1" more height for every 1" more projection, but then puts a 9" mantel at 43-1/2" off the floor.
Gas line connection

Qualified installer only (a licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Connect a listed 1/2" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector to the 1/2" control valve inlet, routed clear of the fan, and leak-check with soapy water.

• Install per local building codes, or ANSI Z223.1 where there are none.
  • Supplied with the stove: a 3/8" x 18" flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. A listed (and Massachusetts-approved) 1/2" tee-handle manual shut-off valve and flexible connector connect to the 1/2" control valve inlet; if substituting, check local codes.
  • Run the gas line to the point where the shut-off valve and flexible line connect (shown on Figure 2.1, p. 9, drawn only). Don't run it where it would obstruct the fan.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests above 1/2 psi: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At 1/2 psi or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or the authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Install the vent system
Use an approved 4" x 6-5/8" co-axial system within the vertical, horizontal or combination limits and the termination clearances. Never connect to a chimney flue serving a solid-fuel appliance.

• Approved makers and caps: Table 6.1 (p. 22). Vertical 4" x 6-5/8" co-axial flexible pipe is not approved. Follow the vent maker's instructions within this manual's limits.
  • Vertical: 36" min to 50' max. Horizontal: 24" vertical allows up to 24" of horizontal run, 36" up to 8', 48" up to 12'. Combination: 25' rise + 25' run = 50' total, inside the shaded area of Figure 6.3 (elbow allowances in the Venting spec).
  • Horizontal sections: 1/4" rise per 12" of travel. Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the stove is installed.
  • Existing chimneys (after inspection by a qualified chimney sweep or professional installer): 4" aluminum flex in a min 7" ID Class A metal/masonry chimney, or 3" x 3" co-linear flex in a min 6" x 8" ID masonry or 7" ID Class A metal chimney.
  • Terminal clearances: section 5.2 (p. 21). Vertical terminal clearances: Figures 5.1–5.3 (p. 20).
Barrier, glass & log set
Place the 8-piece #LX22-500 log set (LX1–LX8) on its log plate, studs, pins and ash-panel notches, spread the rock wool embers, then latch the glass frame and hang the safety barrier.

1. If converting to propane, finish the conversion before the logs go in. Each log is numbered.
  2. Base logs (Figure 7.3): LX1 on the rear log plate; LX2 with its holes on the studs on the left side of the burner; LX3 into the notch in the ash panel; LX4 with its holes on the studs on the right side of the burner.
  3. Top logs (Figure 7.4): LX5 on the left pin of LX1 and the notch in LX2; LX6 on the middle pin of LX1 and the notch in the middle of the ash panel; LX7 on the right pin of LX1 and the notch on the right side of the ash panel; LX8 into its ash-panel notch.
  4. Distribute rock wool embers onto the logs and burner with a stiff or steel bristle nylon brush.
  5. Glass frame: tilt the top forward, align it with the bottom frame rail, and pull the 2 latch assemblies onto the flange on top of the glass valance with the provided tool.
  6. Safety barrier: align the notched tabs on its back with the slots in the stove frame, raise it slightly into the slots and let the tabs lower into position.
Don't place logs directly over burner portholes — it can affect the flame and cause excessive soot on the logs and glass. Never operate the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
Fan kit (LXL-22-MV option)

The fan kit is standard on the LXL-22-L (#LX22-028). On the LXL-22-MV, a qualified installer fits the optional #LX22-028MV kit: fan assembly, speed control box on the gas valve bracket, temperature switch on the firebox floor.

1. Shut off the household breaker before working on any electrical lines.
  2. Remove the cover plate and keep its screws (Figure 7.6).
  3. Mount the fan assembly on the existing holes in the back and underneath of the unit with the 5 screws removed (Figure 7.7).
  4. Mount the speed control box on the right side of the gas valve bracket with the 2 black Phillips head screws included (Figure 7.8).
  5. Place the temperature control switch (magnet attached) on the firebox floor on the right, as far back toward the fan motor as possible (Figure 7.9).
  6. Plug the fan cord into the electrical box receptacle, and the speed control box cord (5 ft) into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle. An outlet near the stove is recommended.
  7. Counterclockwise until it clicks is OFF; clockwise past the click is ON at the highest setting.

The fan runs only once the speed control is ON and the temperature switch has heated; it then turns on and off with the stove's heat.
Electrical

Junction box: 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps — on the LXL-22-L the supply stays hot with no switch. Ground per code into a grounded three-prong receptacle; an optional thermostat or wall switch runs on low-voltage wires.
Initialize the control (LXL-22-L)

Clear packaging from the firebox; rocker switch OFF; 4 AA backup and 3 AAA remote batteries; AC power on; press the sync button (3 beeps, amber LED), then the remote's ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps).

1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox.
  2. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF. Install 4 AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder on the control module and the 3 AAA batteries (components packet) in the remote's battery bay. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  3. Lift the safety barrier screen out of its slots and remove the bottom frame piece; slide out the control module to reach the remote sync button. From here the pilot starts up in manual mode: the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot lights if gas is supplied.
  4. Press the sync button: 3 beeps and an amber LED mean the receiver is ready.
  5. Within 5 seconds, press ON/OFF on the remote: 4 beeps, and the pilot lights automatically.
  6. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command. The system is initialized.
  7. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation and reinstall the safety barrier screen.

LXL-22-MV: light it per its lighting-instructions page (p. 45, not reproduced here); operating notes on p. 46.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet pressure at the IN tap (other gas appliances on) and manifold pressure at the OUT tap, then reseal both: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten each tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten), relight and reattach the manometer; it should read no pressure (each model's steps are in the pressure specs). Flames start blue and turn yellow over the first 15 minutes; then adjust the venturi or vent restriction if needed.

• Inlet (IN tap, A) and manifold (OUT tap, B) values and procedures: see the Inlet and Manifold pressure specs. To reseal each tap: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten), then relight and reattach the manometer; it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on. The turn-off and relight steps differ by model; the specs give each.
  • Let the stove cool before any adjustment. Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician only: open the control enclosure door below the firebox, loosen the wing nut on the venturi lever, move it right to open the air shutter (more air) or left to close it (less air), and retighten. Slight moves make dramatic changes; the provided adjustment tool resets the factory openings (natural gas 1/4", propane 5/8" open).
  • Table 11.6: dark, orange flame — venturi closed, open it slightly; short, blue flames — venturi open too far, close slightly; lifting (ghosting) flames — gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far: check the manometer and/or open slightly.
  • Vent restriction (vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame): first close the baffle restrictor from its factory position #1 to #5, the most restriction; if the flame turns dark with black tips, set it between #2 and #4. If more is needed, add the restrictor plate from the components packet: remove the safety barrier, glass frame and the baffle's 3 screws, bend the plate's tabs to about 80° and insert it into the 4" exhaust pipe with the tabs toward you, then refit the baffle.
  • Table 11.7: short, flickering flame (excessive draft) — add the restrictor plate, or close the baffle restrictor; lifting or ghosting (insufficient draft) — remove the plate's inner ring(s) or the plate, or open the baffle restrictor. If flames still lift after that and the venting checks out, shut off the gas and call a qualified service technician.
Note: for blue flames that lift off the burner, the LXL-22-L troubleshooting chart says to close the venturi slightly (less air) on p. 56, but the LXL-22-MV chart says to open it slightly (more air) on p. 59. Table 11.6 on p. 49 says close slightly for short blue flames and open slightly for lifting (ghosting) flames.

panels.title: LXL-22-L: pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or run on fully charged backup batteries
Wiring disconnection → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check each shut-off valve between the appliance and the main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot not touching the flame rectification sensor → it must envelop the top of the sensor and reach the burner
Pilot always on → control set to CPI; set it to IPI

panels.title: LXL-22-MV: no spark, or pilot won't stay lit
items: No spark from the piezo button → ground the piezo igniter, tighten its fastener, check the wiring to the electrode
Electrode position → 1/8" gap to the pilot; direct metal contact can arc below the electrode
Sparks but no pilot → no gas: check the shut-off valves and the propane tank
Pilot not impinging on the thermocouple → clean the pilot hood; adjust the pilot at the gas valve
Loose thermocouple → fully inserted, hand tight plus 1/4 turn; reading under 15 millivolts → replace it
Thermopile under 350 millivolts at TH-TP and TP (knob at PILOT) → replace
Frequent pilot outages → fit the pilot shield; set the pilot for maximum impingement on the thermopile

panels.title: Burner won't light or won't stay lit
items: Rocker switch OFF → ON (LXL-22-MV: gas knob at ON too, or the wall switch, remote or thermostat calling for heat)
Gas off or low → check for multiple shut-offs; check the propane tank
Faulty or incorrect wiring, or a plugged burner orifice → correct it; remove the blockage
Pilot not directed onto the burner → see the pilot checks
LXL-22-L remote dead or no call for heat → replace batteries; remote ON with thermostat operation OFF
LXL-22-L no reaction to commands → low batteries, remote not paired (reprogram it), or too many failed ignitions (reset the IFC module)
LXL-22-MV switching device → jumper the switch terminals, then the gas valve's switch terminals, to find a bad switch or wiring
LXL-22-MV burner won't stay lit → thermopile wires loose or pinched; refractory panels not tight to the firebox walls

panels.title: Goes out while running, soot, or lifting flames
items: Goes out: no propane; glass frame installed incorrectly; vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked
Goes out: horizontal venting without 1/4" rise per 12"; exhaust leaking back into the firebox; excessive draft → fit or modify the restrictor plate
LXL-22-MV goes out: thermopile or thermocouple not producing proper millivolts
Soot on glass: logs out of place → reset per section 7.3; venturi may need opening slightly (more air)
Soot or lifting: vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked; vent pipes leaking
Blue flame lifting off the burner: the LXL-22-L chart says close the venturi slightly (p. 56); the LXL-22-MV chart says open it slightly (p. 59)

codes: Backup pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF commands. Replace the batteries.
No flame after 2 tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset, or re-initialize (section 9.2).

light.title: Lighting the LXL-22-L (remote model)
light.html:
The LXL-22-L lights itself. Its control sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner.

Everyday start

  1. Check that the main ON/OFF rocker switch is ON. It sits on the left side, behind the safety barrier screen, and must be ON for the remote to run the burner.
  2. With the stove off, press ON/OFF on the remote. The stove beeps once and starts its lighting sequence.
  3. About 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot.

If no flame is sensed within about 60 seconds, it waits about 35 seconds and tries once more. After two failed tries it locks out. See "Won't light? Reset it."

Turning it off

Press ON/OFF again. The remote screen then shows only the room temperature, and the burner goes out. In CPI mode (snowflake icon) the pilot stays lit; in IPI mode it goes out too.

No remote?

The stove can be reset for manual operation (section 9.3, p. 39). The pilot then lights by itself, and the rocker switch turns the burner on and off — on HI only.

If a wall switch or wired thermostat was added, the rocker switch has to stay OFF for it to work, unless its wires were disconnected. When the rocker switch is ON, the burner runs until the rocker switch turns it off.

The manual also has an operating-instructions page for this model (p. 38) that isn't reproduced here. Read it before first use.

lightMv.title: Lighting the LXL-22-MV (millivolt model)
lightMv.html:
The LXL-22-MV has a pilot you light yourself, using the gas control knob on the gas valve and a piezo spark button. Its millivolt gas valve doesn't need house power to operate.

Where the controls are

  • Open the control compartment access panel to reach the gas valve, the gas control knob and the HI/LO knob.
  • The ON/OFF rocker switch is at the rear of the stove.

Lighting the pilot

The step-by-step lighting instructions, with the safety information to read first, are on their own page of the manual (p. 45) and aren't reproduced here. Follow them exactly.

Everyday use

  • Once you've turned the stove on at the gas control knob, the rocker switch turns the burner on and off.
  • Rocker switch OFF turns off only the burner. The pilot stays lit.
  • For more or less flame and heat, turn the HI/LO knob clockwise toward HI or counterclockwise toward LO.
  • If a wall switch or thermostat was added, leave the rocker switch OFF so it can work. With the rocker switch ON, the stove stays on whatever the wall switch or thermostat says.
7-day timeout valve: in regions that require it, the valve turns the burner and pilot off after 7 days with no use. The knob stays where it was (PILOT or ON), so you have to cycle the system by hand to relight it. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day count starts over.

remote.title: Using the remote (LXL-22-L)
remote.html:
The remote takes 3 AAA batteries in the bay at its base. Before first use it is paired with the stove (section 9.2, p. 39).

The everyday keys

  • ON/OFF turns the stove on (the stove beeps once) and off.
  • Up and Down arrows pick one of 6 flame levels. Down lowers one level at a time until the flame is off. Press Up while the stove is on but the flame is off, and it lights on HI.
  • Thermostat key turns the remote into a room thermostat. Set the temperature with the arrows. Press it until SMART shows, and the flame turns itself down as the room reaches your setting. You can't set the flame by hand while SMART is on.
  • Mode key steps to the fan icon. Then the arrows turn the fan on or off and pick one of 6 speeds.

Pilot mode: IPI or CPI

With the stove off, press Mode until the CPI icon shows. Up turns CPI on; Down returns to IPI. In CPI the pilot stays lit (a snowflake icon shows). That keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft so the burner lights with less disruption. After 7 days without the burner lighting, the pilot turns off.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and Up together. A lock icon shows.
  • °F or °C: with the stove off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
  • A battery icon means the remote batteries are low.

normal.title: That's probably normal
normal.html:
Blue flames at first

Right after the burner lights, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow, and should then burn steady, not lifting or floating. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, a qualified service technician may need to adjust the burner's air setting.

Your flame looks different

Flame height and look vary with how the stove is vented and which gas it burns. A stove vented straight up may show an active, compact flame.

Ticks, creaks and some discoloration

Some minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts can make noise. The warranty calls that, and some discoloration, normal — not a defect.

A short pause once a day (LXL-22-L)

Within 24 hours of the pilot staying lit continuously, the control turns off for about 5 seconds to run a safety check. Then it repeats your last command.

The pilot went out by itself

After 7 days without the burner lighting, the pilot turns off on an LXL-22-L in CPI mode, and on an LXL-22-MV fitted with the 7-day timeout valve.

The fan starts late and runs on

In thermostat mode (LXL-22-L), the fan waits 5 minutes after the stove lights and keeps running about 12 minutes after it turns off.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a yearly homeowner job. Never clean it while it's hot.

  1. Set up a flat, stable work area big enough for the glass frame.
  2. Lift the safety barrier screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Find the 2 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox. Use the tool that came with the stove to unlatch them from the flange on top of the glass frame.
  4. Tilt the top of the glass frame forward and lift it off the bottom frame rail.
  5. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  6. To put it back, tilt the top forward, line it up with the bottom frame rail, and use the tool to pull both latches onto the flange. Then reinstall the safety screen.
Don't run the stove without the safety screen, or with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Don't strike or slam the glass. Replacement glass comes from Hussong only as a complete assembly, fitted by a licensed or qualified service person.
Note: p. 29 puts the 2 glass latches at the top of the firebox, but the yearly firebox check on p. 60 refers to a bottom latch assembly.

fan.title: The fan
fan.html:
LXL-22-L: standard, run from the remote

  • Press Mode until the fan icon shows. Then use the arrows to turn it on or off, or pick one of 6 speeds.
  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the stove lights, so heat can build, and keeps running about 12 minutes after the stove turns off.
  • Manual mode: the fan runs at its last setting, with no delay at start or stop.
  • It doesn't run during a power outage.

LXL-22-MV: optional fan kit

  • The kit (#LX22-028MV) is installed by a qualified installer and plugs into a grounded three-prong outlet.
  • Turn the speed knob counterclockwise until it clicks. That's OFF. Turn it clockwise past the click to switch it on at the highest setting, then adjust the speed while it runs.
  • Once switched on, the fan starts and stops by itself as the stove heats up and cools down.
Once a year a qualified service person unplugs the fan and vacuums it. The bearings are sealed and need no oil.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
LXL-22-L

It runs on house power, with a battery backup pack on the control module.

Backup pack4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)
  • In a power outage, the burner and flame height still work on the backup batteries. The fan and accent light kit don't.
  • When the backup batteries run low, the stove double-beeps when you press ON/OFF, and the red light on the control module blinks once, over and over. It won't take commands until you replace them. With fresh ones in, it beeps once.
  • A battery icon on the remote screen means the remote's batteries are low.
  • How long batteries last depends on their quality, how often the stove lights, and similar things.
The LXL-22-L's power supply must stay on at all times. It must not have a switch installed in it.

LXL-22-MV

The millivolt gas valve doesn't need house power to operate. Only the optional fan kit uses 120 volts.

reset.title: Won't light? Reset it
reset.html:
LXL-22-L: lockout

Each time it's turned on, the control tries twice to light the pilot. Each try sparks for about 60 seconds, with about 35 seconds between tries. If both fail, it locks out. The red light on the control module then blinks 3 times, over and over, until it's reset.

Reset it any one of these ways. The lighting sequence then starts again.

  • Rocker switch: set it to OFF, wait about 2 seconds, set it back to ON.
  • Remote: press ON/OFF to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds, press ON/OFF again.
  • Flame arrows: press Down until the screen shows OFF, wait about 2 seconds, then press Up.

Red light blinking 2 times means a pilot flame error: contact your dealer. Blinking once means the backup batteries are low.

Quick checks

  • Is the gas on? There may be more than one shut-off valve. On propane, check the tank.
  • LXL-22-L: rocker switch ON, fresh remote batteries, remote ON and thermostat operation off.
  • LXL-22-MV: gas control knob at ON and rocker switch ON, or the wall switch, remote or thermostat calling for heat.
Anything beyond these checks is for a qualified technician.

safety.title: Safety & yearly service
safety.html:
• The viewing glass gets hot. The barrier screen that comes with the stove reduces the risk of burns and must be installed, to protect children and other at-risk people. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong's barrier for this stove.
  • Any screen or barrier taken off for service goes back on before you use the stove.
  • Keep the stove out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies.
  • Keep the area clear of anything that burns, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.
  • If any part of the stove has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

Yearly service

Have the stove inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. Lint from carpet, bedding and the like can mean cleaning more often. Each year the service person:

  • vacuums the firebox and checks that the latch assembly moves freely,
  • unplugs and vacuums the fan,
  • checks the vent and vent cap for soot or blockage,
  • inspects the glass for cracks, scratches and nicks,
  • vacuums the burner system, checks gas connections for leaks, and watches the pilot and flames in operation.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s limited lifetime warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship, for the original purchaser, from the date of purchase. You don't need to send in any documents to register. Keep your proof of purchase with the stove's serial number and model.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is paid to authorized dealers only. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, run and maintained as the manual says.
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the stove altered or tampered with.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
  • Not covered: normal wear, chimney parts and non-Hussong accessories, venting or site problems, and how well it heats a space.

A part repaired or replaced under warranty is covered for the rest of the original term. A replacement part repaired after the warranty ends gets 90 days of parts coverage.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas min / max5" / 10" WC
Natural gas recommended7" WC
Propane min / max11" / 13" WC

Same for both models (Tables 2.1, 4.1–4.2, 11.1 and 11.3). Test at the valve's IN tap (A) with all other gas appliances in the house on, or at full capacity: loosen the tap screw counterclockwise and attach a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose.

  • LXL-22-L: light pilot and burner and check the reading; turn both off, disconnect the hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten); relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to tap A to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.
  • LXL-22-MV: light the pilot, turn the gas control knob to ON (the burner shouldn't light) and note the reading; rocker switch ON and check the pressure is near maximum inlet pressure; rocker OFF, knob OFF; disconnect the hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten); relight the pilot and turn the knob to ON, then reattach the manometer to tap A to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.

Too high or too low: contact the gas company — only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure. Supply-piping tests above 1/2 psi: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at 1/2 psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.html:

Same for both models (Tables 2.1, 11.2 and 11.4). Test at the valve's OUT tap (B): light the pilot, loosen the tap screw counterclockwise and attach a manometer on a 1/4" I.D. hose, then bring on the burner (LXL-22-L: light the burner; LXL-22-MV: gas control knob to ON, rocker switch ON) and read. LXL-22-L: turn burner and pilot off. Both models: disconnect the manometer hose and tighten the tap clockwise, snug without over-tightening, then attach the manometer to the OUT tap (B) to verify it is completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Flame appearance also depends on altitude, fuel quality and venting — see the pressure test & flame check step for venturi and restrictor settings.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
4" exhaust x 6-5/8" air intake co-axial. Approved makers (horizontal and vertical terminations): American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab, Olympia Chimney Supply, Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent — caps in Table 6.1. Vertical 4" x 6-5/8" co-axial flexible pipe is not approved.

Horizontal (vertical pipe + 90° elbow + cap)

24" verticalup to 24" horizontal
36" verticalup to 8' horizontal
48" verticalup to 12' horizontal

Vertical: 36" min to 50' max + termination cap.

Combination: the termination must fall inside the shaded area of Figure 6.3 (a diagram, p. 25); 25' max rise + 25' max run = 50' total. Max 5 × 90° elbows — subtract 3' for each one after the first. 2 × 45° may replace one 90°; subtract 18" per 45°.

Chimney conversions — have the existing chimney inspected by a qualified chimney sweep or professional installer, and confirm the local jurisdiction allows it. Both allow 0" to 24" of horizontal run and 10' min to 50' max of aluminum flex:

  • 4" flex in an existing min 7" ID Class A metal/masonry chimney: 90° elbow + 24" max horizontal + retro connector + 4" flex + top adapter + cap. Install the vent heat shield assembly when using minimum horizontal venting off the top of the stove.
  • 3" x 3" co-linear flex (with a 4" x 6-5/8" reducer) in a min 6" x 8" ID masonry or 7" ID Class A metal chimney: 90° elbow + 24" max horizontal + co-axial to co-linear adapter + 3" x 3" flex + roof flashing + cap.
Never connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid-fuel appliance. Horizontal sections need 1/4" rise per 12" of travel. Avoid tight bends in flex pipe. Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after installation.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC · 60Hz · 6 Amps
LXL-22-L backup4 × AA (burner and flame height only)

  • Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Ground per local codes, or ANSI/NFPA 70 (CSA C22.1 in Canada). The three-prong plug goes into a properly grounded receptacle — never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • LXL-22-L: the AC supply must be hot at all times with no switch installed in it; the system runs on 120 VAC and/or batteries. An optional thermostat or wall switch can run the main burner on low-voltage wires (thermostat wire not included). Either disconnect the rocker switch wires from the control module, or leave the rocker switch OFF — when ON, the burner runs until the rocker switch turns it off, and the thermostat or wall switch can't.
  • LXL-22-MV: the millivolt valve needs no 120 VAC — never connect 120 VAC to the gas valve. The optional component connection is for low-voltage battery or DC only; the fan kit (#LX22-028MV) is the only part on 120 volts. An optional thermostat or wall switch runs on low-voltage wires (not included); the rocker switch overrides it unless it is OFF or its wire is disconnected from the back of the gas valve. An optional remote receiver mounting bracket fits the control compartment with 2 screws.

Wiring diagrams: Figure 8.1 (LXL-22-L, p. 36) and Figure 8.2 (LXL-22-MV, p. 37), drawn only. Mount any wall control or thermostat on a wall near the stove.

conflicts.issue: LXL-22-L propane conversion kit: section 3.1 cites the #LCK-LX22L-S30 conversion kit manual, while the LXL-22-L parts list gives 'S.I.T. Conversion Kit - Propane LCK-LX22-S30'. The parts list settles it: its natural gas kit is NCK-LX22-S30, and the same p. 11 sentence cites the LXL-22-MV kit manual by its parts-list number (OCK-S190A, p. 64). Card and drawer show LCK-LX22-S30, with a small note giving p. 11's LCK-LX22L-S30.

Masonry application mantel heights: 3/4" trim from 40-1/2" and a 6" mantel from 44" above the floor, with 1" more height per 1" more projection (a 9" mantel 3" higher than the minimum), yet the same paragraph puts the 9" mantel at 43-1/2" off the floor — lower than the 6" mantel. Also flagged in step2.

Remedy for blue flames lifting off the burner: the LXL-22-L troubleshooting chart says close the venturi air shutter slightly (less air); the LXL-22-MV chart says open it slightly (more air). Table 11.6 gives close slightly for short blue flames (venturi open too far) and open slightly for lifting/ghosting flames (venturi closed too far); the 11.3.1 text says opening the shutter causes a short blue flame that may lift. Also noted in the last faults panel.

Glass latch location: 7.2.1 says 2 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox secure the glass assembly, while the 13.1 annual firebox check says to inspect and operate the bottom latch assembly.

review.notes: One guide covers both versions: LXL-22-L (Proflame 2 IFC, IPI with CPI option, remote, 120 VAC + AA backup, fan standard) and LXL-22-MV (millivolt valve, piezo-lit pilot, gas control knob, rear rocker switch, HI/LO knob, optional 7-day timeout valve, fan kit optional); ignition-specific content is labeled per model. Pages 2, 4 and 6 are blank. Page 38 ('9.0 Operating Instructions - LXL-22-L') and page 45 ('10.0 Operating Instructions - OAK-18-MV', the lighting instructions per p. 46) carry only their headings in the text — presumably images. So the LXL-22-MV lighting procedure is not transcribed (the lightMv drawer sends owners to p. 45), and there is no 'if you smell gas' drawer or index entry: no gas-smell text exists elsewhere in the manual. Drawings only, not transcribed: appliance dimensions (Figure 2.1, p. 9) and safety-barrier dimensions (Figure 2.2, p. 10); horizontal rough-in (3.2), alcove framing (3.3–3.4), masonry layout (3.5), outdoor overhang (3.6–3.7), combination-vent shaded area (6.3), wiring diagrams (8.1–8.2), log placement and venturi-tool figures. Not in the manual text, so not checked against the catalog: height/width/depth (32 / 30.8125 / 20.6875 in), weight (207 lb), view area (16" x 22" — the only glass size in the text is the 23.625" x 18" glass part, p. 65), efficiency (70.1 / 70.33 AFUE), heating area; catalog features 'ceramic glass', 'traditional legs' and 'brick or black glass panels' aren't mentioned (the manual only says 'refractory or panel set (if installed)'). Catalog model_numbers is empty; the manual's are LXL-22-L and LXL-22-MV. Roof-pitch table (p. 20): only 'Flat to 6/12 = 1.0 ft' keeps its pitch label in the text, so the 1.25–8.0 ft rows aren't given. Section 6.4.2 (p. 24) labels the 36" and 48" configurations 'Minimum'/'Maximum Horizontal' inconsistently, but the run lengths (24", 8', 12') are unambiguous. Section 7.1's '(4) slots located on each side' is ambiguous (4 total or 4 per side), so the guide gives no slot count. Slips left out of the guide: 9.9.5 'Turn OFF the appliance' (p. 42) repeats the turn-on wording (the guide uses its stated result — the burner turns off); Table 4.2 (p. 19) is titled 'LXL-22-L (Millivolt)' (same values as LXL-22-MV Table 11.3); Tables 11.2/11.4 label the manifold row 'Inlet Pressure Tap (B)'; troubleshooting cites an 'OP18-500' log set (pp. 55, 59) for the LX22-500; p. 59 prints 12" as 30mm; p. 11 points to section 3.4 for horizontal framing (the rough-in is on p. 13) and chapter 3 section numbers don't match the TOC; 'Metal Fab*' and 'section 6.1.1' (p. 22) have no footnote or section; outdoor wiring cites 'NECA NFPA 70' (guide: NFPA 70). Manifold kPa equivalents differ slightly between Table 2.1 (0.40 / 0.875 / 2.49 kPa, p. 8) and Tables 11.2/11.4 (0.41 / 0.87 / 2.48 kPa, pp. 47–48); in. WC values agree and the guide uses in. WC only. Possibly inconsistent, not used in the guide: burner plate LX22-350 (LXL-22-L, p. 63) vs LX22-035 (LXL-22-MV, p. 64); the MV natural gas and propane control boards share LX22MV-770; the parts list's '36" Black Flex Tube (Gas line to valve) 700-236B' vs the 3/8" x 18" flexible gas connector supplied per 4.2 (p. 19) — may be different parts. The MV inlet test's 'check pressure to ensure it is near maximum inlet pressure' with the rocker switch ON (p. 48) is reproduced as printed. LXL-22-L rocker switch: ON for remote operation (p. 39) but OFF for a wired thermostat/wall switch unless its wires are disconnected (p. 35) — presented as two setups, not a conflict; the MV troubleshooting fix 'rocker ON, wall switch/remote/thermostat calling for heat' (p. 58) is worded as either/or to stay consistent with p. 35. The 'accent light kit' appears only on p. 39 (no such kit in the parts list). The LXL-22-MV manifold test (p. 48, steps 4–7) prints no turn-off step before 'Disconnect manometer hose'; the LXL-22-L test (p. 47, step 5) turns burner and pilot off first. The guide reports each as printed. check_numbers: every number in the guide was found in the manual text; single-digit values were re-checked by hand.
